archetypes.name: state-machine
archetypes.rationale: The two-path design (subprocess vs in-process) and the symlink guard in sync_latest_reviewer_status create ordering-sensitive state; correctness depends on which path clears symlinks and when.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the ordering constraints between _clean_round_dir (which removes the reviewer-status.tsv symlink) and the try_write_reviewer_status_tsv calls in plan_review.py _run_round_body. The subprocess path first removes the symlink via _clean_round_dir, then runs the subprocess, then conditionally materializes. Verify: if the subprocess itself writes a reviewer-status.tsv symlink (not a regular file), the post-subprocess guard checks is_file() which is false for a dangling symlink but can be true for a valid symlink — confirm this does not cause the fallback materializer to skip when it should run. In the in-process execute_round path (plan_review_round.py), _clean_round_dir is never called, so a pre-existing symlink at round_dir/reviewer-status.tsv causes write_reviewer_status_tsv to return None at the is_symlink() guard (line ~272). Check whether that silent skip is safe or if the caller should be removing the symlink before calling. Also check sync_latest_reviewer_status: it returns early if latest.is_symlink() without removing it, meaning a stale symlink at latest-reviewer-status.tsv permanently blocks all future syncs — verify there is a removal path for that symlink somewhere, or flag the gap. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
